The overall global deposits of the bank increased 16.4% year-on-year to reach ₹17.45 lakh crore. Domestic deposits also saw a marked increase of 16.6%, driven by term deposits growing 20.5%. Additionally, the bank reported a 35.8% rise in standalone net profit for the second quarter of FY27.

banking-economy.title: Bank credit growth outpaces deposits at 17.94% as festive demand picks up
banking-economy.summary: Bank credit expanded significantly, reaching Rs 232.54 lakh crore by mid-October 2026, showing a strong 17.94 percent growth. In contrast, bank deposits increased to Rs 284.37 lakh crore, marking a 16.60 percent rise. This growth was fueled by increased liquidity in the banking system and festive season demand. Additionally, commercial banks saw a 9.64 percent rise in government securities, totaling Rs 77.32 lakh crore.

banking-economy.title: Banks must go beyond lending to unlock Bengal's industrial potential: NITI Aayog's Ashok Lahiri
banking-economy.summary: NITI Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Lahiri emphasized the need for banks to facilitate connections between businesses and financial resources. He pointed out the low credit-deposit ratio in Eastern India, which hinders investment and economic growth. Lahiri highlighted the importance of investment in infrastructure, industrial expansion, and the MSME sector. Banks could support smaller enterprises with structured credit facilities to help them grow.
